title: Capstone: build and ship a real application
audience: a computer science graduate or an experienced self-taught programmer preparing for and starting a software engineering job
purpose: Plan, build and ship a complete application as a professional would: choosing and scoping a project, milestones and a backlog, repository setup and code review, continuous integration, configuration and secrets, containers, deployment and continuous delivery, logging and monitoring, performance, security and accessibility review, documentation, a demo and a retrospective.

weeks.2: Planning: milestones, issues and a backlog
weeks.3: Repository setup, branching and code review
weeks.4: Continuous integration: automated tests and checks

blocks.deliverable: Write a one-page project proposal and a backlog.
Set up a CI pipeline that runs the tests.
Week 7 midterm; deploy the first working version.
Add monitoring and fix three issues found in review.
Give a demo and write a retrospective.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Ship it: a complete deployed application with a repository, a CI/CD pipeline, a test suite, a container, monitoring, a README and architecture notes, a recorded or live demo, and a retrospective on what you would do differently.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
